title: Material alteration: surprise and hardship
summary: A material alteration is an added term whose incorporation without express awareness would cause the kind of surprise or hardship addressed by § 2-207(2)(b) and its commentary.
notes:
Bayway places the burden on the party resisting an additional term in a transaction between merchants. It examines both actual surprise and what a reasonable merchant should have expected in the industry. The court leaves open whether hardship is an independent basis because the buyer’s evidence was insufficient either way. The casebook records variation in the treatment of particular clauses. The size of an invoice or a party’s assertion that it did not read a term does not by itself answer the materiality question.

Bayway requires attention to subjective and objective surprise and holds that industry practice defeated the claimed objective surprise. It expressly declines to decide whether hardship is an independent ground because the evidence was insufficient either way. Union Carbide’s quoted view treats hardship as a consequence rather than a separate criterion. Some cases deem particular terms material categorically; Dorton treats its arbitration question as fact dependent. Preserve those differences.
